p: Get thee out of thy country: From the flood to this time were four hundred and twenty-three years.
a land that I will shew: In appointing him no certain place, he proves so much more his faith and obedience.
a blessing: The world shall recover by your seed, which is Christ, the blessing which they lost in Adam.
souls that they had gotten in: Meaning servants as well as cattle.
passed through the land unto the: He wandered to and fro in the land before he could find a settling place: thus God exercises the faith of his children.
Canaanite was then in the land: Which was a cruel and rebellious nation, by whom God kept his in continual exercise.
an altar unto the LORD: It was not enough for him to worship God in his heart, but it was expedient to declare by outward profession his faith before men, of which this altar was a sign.
thence unto a mountain on the: Because of the troubles that he had among that wicked people.
altar unto the LORD: And so served the true God, and renounced all idolatry.
And Abram journeyed: Thus the children of God may look for no rest in this world, but must wait for the heavenly rest and quietness.
famine in the land: This was a new trial of Abram's faith: by which we see that the end of one affliction is the beginning of another.

sister: By this we learn not to use unlawful means nor to put others in danger to save ourselves, Ge 12:20. Though it may appear that Abram did not fear death, so much as dying without children, he acts as though God's promise had not taken place; in which appeared a weak faith.
taken into Pharaoh's house: To be his wife.
plagued Pharaoh and his house with: The Lord took the defence of this poor stranger against a mighty king: and as he is ever careful over his, so did he preserve Sarai.
commanded his men concerning him: To the intent that none should hurt him either in his person or goods.
